title: Friends dancing to jazz without seeing it as art
summary: Harold Bartell learned piano from Piron's pianist; most of her crowd enjoyed jazz without realizing a culture was being born.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, among your friends, back in the 20s, did most of them just think of something to go dance to and have a good time to it? Did any of them...

Well, I'm afraid we... No, I... Harold Bartell was more interested in our craft than others, because he played the piano, and he played by ear like Steve, who was Perron's piano player, who was so well-known. And in fact, Steve gave him lessons, because he was interested in how. And I imagine... And of course, my sister and I, who sang a lot, were interested in the harmonizing part of it. But most of them, I would say, were not as devoted in jazz clubs as Menville and Soucha and all of them are today. It was so comparatively new that we accepted it as that and didn't realize what history it was making at the time.
What about... You know what you said, we didn't think of it as an art form.
Not to my regulation. I mean, we were all interested in learning. Learning it.
And following, but we had no idea that a real culture was being born right there in front of our eyes.
